- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 10% above recent peak), apply mean reversion bias: subtract 5–8% from next 3 periods to prevent overhang.  
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.6), model should adjust forecast mid-horizon to reflect sentiment reversal, not wait for full 30d decay.  
- If forecast mean is consistently 2–3% above true outcome over 30d, apply downward bias adjustment to next forecast window — especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.  
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., first 5–7 days drop after peak), model should anticipate this and adjust forecast downward earlier than true trend.
